messages:
cust_alex: Hey team — after the reserved-capacity pin this morning our embeddings dropped from 1536 -> 1024. Downstream index (Annoy) throws shape errors. Sample response below, ticket SUP-10321.

support_alan: Sorry you're hit by this, Alex. Can you paste the exact model param you pinned and one sample response (curl output) so we can confirm the shape? Also, any request_id from the failing API calls?

cust_alex: Sure — we pinned model=open-embed-large:2026-03-17 and the app calls /v1/embeddings. Example curl and truncated response:

```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-embed-large:2026-03-17","input":"hello world"}'
```
Response: {"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.23, ..., 0.12],"index":0}],"model":"open-embed-large:2026-03-17"} — vector length = 1024 (we previously received 1536). Request IDs: r_ae12f3, r_ae12f4.

eng_michelle: Thanks Alex. Two quick hypotheses: 1) The pinned variant actually pointed to a 1024-quantized build (variant aliasing), or 2) smart routing/fallback sent requests to a compatible lower-dim variant during capacity pressure. Can you confirm the pin target is a specific immutable version (sha) vs an alias?

ops_sam: Noted — we've observed cases where reserved pools with mixed variants trigger an automated fallback to a lower-dim variant when the original device type wasn't available. Deploybot logs show an auto-rollback on the canary around timestamp 6187654320. That aligns with your first failing requests.

deploybot: System: Canary auto-roll performed -> fallback variant open-embed-medium (1024) due to GPU capacity threshold breach at 6187654320.

support_alan: Short-term mitigations: 1) Re-pin to explicit immutable model version (sha) to avoid alias resolution. 2) If you need 1536 vectors, repopulate your index with the new vectors or roll back to the previous pinned version. 3) Confirm the response vector length in CI by adding a quick check: `len(response.data[0].embedding)`.

eng_michelle: Repro steps for our side to validate:
1) Use your exact pinned value and run 100 parallel embedding calls against reserved pool.
2) Capture router logs for request_ids r_ae12f3 and r_ae12f4.
3) Check routing policy table for fallbacks mapping (embed_dim -> compatible_variants).

support_alan: Quick CLI checks you can run now:
```
# verify dim
python -c "import requests; r=requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'open-embed-large:2026-03-17','input':'x'}); print(len(r.json()['data'][0]['embedding']))"
```
If it prints 1024, repin or reindex. We can also force route via `?force_variant=sha:abcdef` in the short term (ops can enable).

cust_alex: Got it — we'll pin to the immutable sha and kick an index rebuild. Please escalate if you see any other auto-fallbacks for our org. Thanks. :thumbsup:

ops_sam: Logged escalation under ops-incident-594. We'll pull router traces and confirm whether fallback triggers are overly permissive for reserved pools.

support_alan: I'll follow up with a quick note in the ticket with requested logs and a recommended rollback/reindex path. If you want, we can schedule a brief call to coordinate reindexing to avoid downtime.

cust_alex: Appreciate it, team. Scheduling call now.
